680ed400.task:
Perform comprehensive reconnaissance and attack-surface mapping of the in-scope web application at http://host.docker.internal:4175 (black-box, no source code available).

Objectives:
1. HTTP probing & tech fingerprinting: use httpx (headers, server, cookies, technologies, TLS info) and curl to identify the framework, server software, and versions. Note any WAF/fingerprint quirks.
2. Thorough crawling: use katana (bounded depth, e.g. -d 3) and/or agent-browser (use --session recon-mapping for an isolated browser session) to enumerate all pages, links, forms, API endpoints, JS files, and hidden paths. Interact with any login/registration/search features found. Extract endpoints from JS files too.
3. Directory/file enumeration: run ffuf with a reasonable wordlist (e.g. /usr/share/wordlists/dirb/common.txt or seclists if present) against the target to find hidden paths. Keep it bounded and tidy: store raw output under /workspace/recon/ and remove bulky intermediates once endpoints are extracted.
4. Parameter discovery: use arjun (or manual analysis) on key endpoints to find hidden parameters.
5. Capture everything through the Caido proxy (env vars already route traffic through it) so the traffic history is available to other agents. Do NOT delete captured traffic.
6. Analyze responses for interesting signals: error pages, debug endpoints, admin panels, API docs (swagger/openapi), version disclosure, default credentials hints, interesting cookies (names/flags), auth mechanisms (JWT, sessions), and any user roles.

Deliverable: a comprehensive report via agent_finish containing:
- Technology stack & versions
- Full endpoint inventory (method, path, parameters, auth required or not) — include a machine-readable endpoint list saved to /workspace/recon/endpoints.txt
- Forms and their actions/fields
- Cookie/session/JWT details
- Authentication and authorization model as observed (login/register roles, admin areas)
- Any interesting findings or anomalies worth deeper testing
- Clean up raw crawler output after extracting the endpoint list (keep /workspace/recon/endpoints.txt and a concise notes file)
